sections.title: A new job for a familiar prefix
sections.content: felír ("to prescribe", literally "to write up") is built from the coverb fel- you already met in the imperative unit, plus ír ("to write"). In a plain statement like this, the coverb stays attached right before the verb: Az orvos felír egy receptet ("the doctor writes/prescribes a prescription").

items.spanish: Az orvos felír nekem egy receptet.
items.english: The doctor prescribes me a prescription.

sections.content: recept means "prescription" here, the very same word you already know as "recipe" from the cooking unit — Hungarian uses one word for both a recipe and a doctor's prescription.
